dropped.claim: Adaptive Biotechnologies operates two businesses: MRD (minimal residual disease testing via clonoSEQ) and Immune Medicine (TCR/BCR data licensing and discovery). MRD revenue reached $212.3M in 2025, growing 46% and driving total revenue to $277.0M (up 54.8% YoY). Operating losses narrowed dramatically from $162.5M in 2024 to $57.1M in 2025, while operating cash burn halved to $46.0M. However, the company remains deeply unprofitable with a $1.4B accumulated deficit, holds only $70.5M cash against $126.6M debt, faces structural reimbursement risk where payors can retroactively recoup payments without recourse, and exhibits revenue volatility (revenue fell from $185.3M in 2022 to $170.3M in 2023 before recovering). Growth depends on expanding clonoSEQ into new indications and sample types—an uncertain effort—and on the unproven Immune Medicine platform monetizing proprietary datasets of 100,000+ disease signatures and 5,000,000+ TCR-antigen matches through deals like the December 2025 Pfizer agreements.

The Immune Medicine business possesses proprietary datasets of over 100,000 cancer and autoimmune disease signatures and more than 5,000,000 TCR-to-antigen matches spanning over 20,000 antigens, recently monetized through two non-exclusive Pfizer agreements in December 2025 for rheumatoid arthritis and broader immunology applications.
